repository.head: The fix branch contains the qualified GUI simplification, store menu, resource-arbitration regression coverage, and Windows COM1-COM9 serial-lock repair and is ready for a local v0.1.6 distribution rebuild.
repository.remote_head: origin/master remains 9e036db. No push, tag, GitHub Release, updater manifest, or Gitee sync was changed.
repository.working_tree: The fix branch contains the qualified tracked changes plus pre-existing local build, cache, and hardware artifacts that remain outside Git.

mission.product: MKLink/MicroLink tooling for local and authenticated VPN/LAN remote firmware flash, embedded debug, symbols, memory, RTT/SystemView/VOFA/SuperWatch streaming, Serial, Modbus, MCP, Web, Tauri desktop, and standalone Site Agent workflows.
mission.maintenance: Keep this file limited to the current baseline, durable decisions, latest qualification evidence, unresolved limits, and next actions. Git history is the record for completed chronology.

current_session.current_task: Qualified the GUI simplification, dual-store menu, Dashboard resource arbitration, and Windows COM1-COM9 serial-lock repair; commit the fix branch and rebuild the local v0.1.6 installer, Skill, and Web GUI from that stable commit.
current_session.release: The maintainer authorized a standard NSIS rebuild, overwrite installation, matching local Skill update, and same-version Web GUI. The current fix branch must not be merged or pushed implicitly; tag, GitHub Release, updater manifest changes, and Gitee sync remain out of scope.

milestones.name: Product and distribution baseline
milestones.notes: Online/offline flash, debug control, symbols and types, bounded binary streaming, Serial, Modbus, MCP, Web, Tauri v2, bundled Python sidecar, USB Web entry, browser file uploads, updater flow, and resource arbitration are implemented.

milestones.name: Flash, symbols, and RTT correctness
milestones.notes: Builtin pyelftools is authoritative by default; aggregate symbols and bounded pasted C layouts work; symbol reload is a shared device transaction; HPM low-address writable ELF sections can supply _SEGGER_RTT; successful automatic connections backfill the actual serial port; Tauri paths and Chromium file handles detect rebuilt online-flash images, while legacy browser inputs permit same-path manual reload.

milestones.name: HPM5301 ROM API and SuperWatch
milestones.notes: HPM targets use the device ROM API without FLM. SuperWatch uses a fixed-duration oscilloscope timeline that follows live data with an adjustable fixed lag, freezes on pause, and supports retained-history navigation. HPM online flash synchronously stops SuperWatch, closes the shared Device, and releases the probe before programming.

milestones.name: Global GUI localization and navigation
milestones.notes: One persistent Chinese/English switch controls the Web/Tauri shell and embedded waveform workspace. The shell brand is MKLink. Technical English names remain unchanged. Dashboard order is RTT View, SuperWatch, HardFault, Memory, Serial Assistant, Modbus, RTOS Trace, and Symbols last; the user-facing Debug Control tab and detected MCU-family labels are removed while the CLI/API debug surface remains available. The content card starts directly with a compact tab row; the redundant Dashboard heading is removed and the resource-owner status shares that row. A persistent header action provides quick Device connect/disconnect, and each Dashboard surface now explains only its current missing prerequisite with an inline action. RTT View keeps address/source on one row and grouped acquisition, encoding, metrics, and secondary actions on the next; data-format examples open on demand instead of consuming a permanent third row.

milestones.name: Lazy large-array symbol browsing
milestones.notes: Arrays are grouped into 256-direct-element range nodes and expanded on demand. Structure arrays and nested arrays retain their hierarchy; exact backend search resolves unloaded paths; later elements support type lookup and the normal SuperWatch/read/write descriptor path. The old first-256-leaves warning is removed.

milestones.name: HPM5301 SystemView recorder and analysis
milestones.notes: RTOS Trace shares RTT address state with RTT View and uses the probe SystemView bridge plus SEGGER UART Recorder handshake. Delayed TaskList recovery, parser framing recovery, valid HPM ram_base=0/id_shift=0, exact Runtime/Context analysis, inactive task retention, and running-session metadata hydration restore task1/task2/task3/Tmr Svc correctly. Timeline uses a microsecond ruler, 10-second default, 10/30/60-second choices, 300,000-event browser ring, wheel zoom, drag pan, and Fit All. Explicit JSONL recording is independent of display and acquisition; offline replay is bounded and supports pause, speed, progress, and restart.

milestones.name: RTT terminal mode
milestones.notes: RTT remains channel 0 only. Log and terminal subscribers use independent binary hubs and Worker decode paths without restarting target RTT. Terminal chunks decode incrementally into xterm.js and do not construct, synchronize, or mount hidden log rows; Log mode retains at most 5,000 virtualized entries and can save the retained UTF-8 text locally. Common ANSI/SEGGER normalization, convertEol, and batched Down Buffer keyboard writes remain supported; termios, PTY/ConPTY, multi-channel UI, and SEGGER virtual terminals are intentionally out of scope.

milestones.name: Serial Assistant terminal and explicit Device lifecycle
milestones.notes: Serial Assistant provides 日志 and xterm terminal modes without requiring an MKLink target connection. One backend serial hub preserves exact RX/TX bytes, while separate Worker clients decode either bounded structured logs or immediate RX-only terminal chunks. Terminal mode does not construct, synchronize, or mount hidden log rows; Log mode retains at most 5,000 virtualized entries and can save the retained UTF-8 text locally. Explicit Open/Close controls own the serial lifecycle; mode, dashboard-tab, and route changes close only the browser subscription. Serial and RTT keep separate resources, settings, histories, status, and transports. Automated, Web, real-target, and paired-virtual-UART qualification passed.

milestones.name: Offline flash UX and conservative device labeling
milestones.notes: Offline Flash requests include only algorithms referenced by firmware rows, so unused missing FLMs do not block deployment. Selected unavailable FLMs are highlighted and can be replaced with a local upload; common backend failures are translated into actionable guidance with expandable technical details. RTT View and Serial Assistant default to Terminal mode. Header links expose 在线文档 and a responsive 淘宝店铺 menu whose first entry is the existing official store and whose disabled second entry reserves the pending Xianji custom-store link. The STM32F10x profile no longer claims Medium Density from a family-level IDCODE match.

milestones.name: Remote Site Agent and in-process STCP integration
milestones.notes: The standalone field client remains a portable Windows EXE/ZIP with direct WebSocket and in-process LAN STCP. The pending v0.1.6 main Tauri GUI adds a native-only Site Agent page and hosts the same listener inside the existing Python sidecar, borrowing the GUI Device and ResourceManager instead of opening a second backend or probe. DPAPI-protected credentials are passed only through the owned child environment; enabled service lifecycle is retained in the tray.

verification.area: v0.1.6 unified main-GUI Site Agent final gate
verification.result: On feature/gui-site-agent-integration from ba56901, full Python passed 1,253 with 1 skipped; full GUI passed 49 files and 494 tests; vue-tsc and Vite 8.1.5 production build passed. Main Tauri Rust passed 10 tests, rustfmt check, and optimized release build. The isolated PyInstaller sidecar build and local health smoke passed. Fresh GEC1900 Windows HIL opened the actual Site Agent page, generated and stored a DPAPI CurrentUser token, applied LAN configuration, and verified a 8766-to-8767-to-8766 restart sequence. The engineer CLI passed health, status, ports, capabilities, reconnect, and probe.info through the LAN Agent. GUI, Agent, and remote call agreed on the same STM32F40x target while sharing one sidecar worker and probe connection. Alt+F4 hid the GUI to tray without stopping either listener or the target connection. Two HIL defects were fixed and regressed: the Windows Job Object now terminates the complete PyInstaller child generation before restart, and restore_last no longer requests symbol parsing when a shared connection has no AXF. The final field runtime was restarted without the temporary WebView debug port, reconnected read-only, and left ready; temporary plaintext token files, CLI site registration, debug environment, and scheduled tasks were removed. No flash, reset, halt, RAM write, register write, or firmware change was performed. The updater private key remains unavailable, so signed NSIS publication is still blocked.

verification.area: Vite WebSocket proxy and source Web regression
verification.result: The source Vite server had proxied only /api since its introduction, while RTT, SuperWatch, SystemView, and VOFA later moved to /ws/streams/*. REST calls therefore remained healthy at port 5173 while binary streams bypassed the backend. vite.config.ts now forwards /ws with WebSocket upgrade enabled to port 8765, and a Node-environment Vitest test pins both /api and /ws proxy contracts. On the real STM32F103RC through http://127.0.0.1:5173, RTT delivered MSH output, 16-channel SuperWatch accumulated 631,520 complete samples around 859 Hz with zero host/target errors or drops, RTOS Trace received about 154,089 events, and a direct VOFA WebSocket handshake reached Open through the Vite proxy.

verification.result: The clean combined-branch Windows Site Agent package had SHA-256 713FD6C34A4232455E42747AB41B2492E5B2B3E3ABDD1D8ADE78D13982E7FAE3 and contained no frpc/frps. Loopback health/status/capabilities/ports, token isolation, reconnect, STM32F10x probe.info, halted registers, confirmed superwatch_ch00 write/read/restore, RTT channel 0 HIL_PING echo, SystemView channel 1 with 8,148 bytes and 1,991 parsed events/tasks, cleanup, site deletion, and port release passed. verification.area: Large-array symbol browsing
verification.result: On the real STM32 AXF, _thread_stack exposed eight 256-element ranges through [1792..2047]. The tail request returned exactly _thread_stack[1792] through _thread_stack[2047], exact search found unloaded _thread_stack[2047], type lookup reported uint8_t at 0x20009A63, and target read returned 35. No write was performed because the available large arrays are active stack/buffer memory; the dynamic write path is covered automatically. SuperWatch and Symbols Web views both rendered only the selected tail page, omitted [0], removed the old warning, and produced no console warnings or errors.

verification.area: HPM5301 flash and dump-memory
verification.result: The hello_world sample rebuilt, programmed, and verified through the HPM ROM API at 0x80000400. One 4-byte region sustained 6,935.9 Hz and three regions totaling 9 bytes sustained 2,416.4 Hz in 30-second runs with no flags, parser warnings, or failures. SuperWatch also accumulated more than 100,000 complete samples without host drops and released the probe before online flash.

verification.area: STM32F103RC dump-memory throughput
verification.result: Keil ARMClang rebuilt and downloaded the STM32F103RC target with no errors or warnings. Separate-region dump-memory sweeps reached about 30.22/16.53/8.87/4.50/2.29 kHz for 1/2/4/8/16 regions; the 16-region 30-second run sustained 2,262.44 Hz with zero flags or mismatches. SuperWatch coalesced 16 contiguous floats into one 64-byte block and rendered all channels at 6,636.66 Hz over 30 seconds with no acquisition, parser, backend, or transport drops; the Hz-only badge matched an independent counter measurement.

verification.area: SuperWatch Web interaction baseline
verification.result: Real STM32 Web tests qualified the complete current interaction model: configurable history up to 1,000,000 points/channel without changing the live span, frozen pause history with pan/zoom/minimap browsing, live X zoom and navigation that preserve a fixed lag while advancing, double-click reset to the newest window, independent split-channel Y axes with shared X, persistent merge control, and an auto-hiding channel legend. The one-request-in-flight Worker envelope scheduler remains responsive near 9.26 kHz, and the tested surfaces produced no transport/backend drops or browser warnings/errors.

verification.result: Builtin ELF resolved HPM low-address _SEGGER_RTT and portable writable variables. RTT auto-search and address sharing worked. The source Web GUI was exercised in Chinese and English at desktop and mobile sizes without relevant console errors or document overflow.

verification.area: Combined STM32F103RC Web and hardware regression
verification.result: On the real STM32F103RC, 16-channel SuperWatch ran in dump-memory mode around 844-858 Hz with zero read, parser, firmware, backend, or transport drops; all 16 curves filled the full canvas, the legend auto-hid, pause retained 200,000 transport samples, changing the history limit from 50,000 to 250,000 points/channel preserved the paused viewport, and stopping kept Device connected. RTT channel 0 accepted help and returned the MSH prompt with zero stream drops. HardFault reported no fault; Memory read 64 bytes at 0x20000000; halt/core-register/resume returned plausible ARM registers and restored execution. SystemView captured 14,320 events and 56,865 bytes in four seconds at 72 MHz, recovered six task names plus SysTick, had no event-packet or target-overflow drops, and stopped cleanly. _thread_stack returned exactly 256 tail elements from [1792] through [2047]. The paired virtual UART passed a synchronized bidirectional REST/OS loop with exact 9-byte TX and 11-byte RX, Modbus returned HTTP 409 while the serial port was occupied without closing Serial Assistant, and explicit Serial stop allowed immediate native reopen.

verification.area: RTT terminal Web and STM32 hardware loop
verification.result: The STM32F103RC test firmware rebuilt with Keil ARMClang without errors or warnings and was downloaded with IDE verify OK. Triggering its controlled ANSI self-test rendered RT-Thread green/yellow/red/magenta log colors, SEGGER normal and bright foreground/background macros, ESC[2K line erase, cursor overwrite, ESC[2J clear/home, and a split CSI sequence in the xterm terminal. Terminal keyboard input reached RTT channel 0 and returned 0d (Enter), 7f (Backspace), and 1b 5b 41 (ArrowUp) through the diagnostic loopback. With the later Agile Console RTT firmware, the real MSH help command emitted bare-LF lines that all rendered from column zero; the prompt and consecutive rows had no staircase or extra blank lines, while Log mode retained all 37 raw rows. Log/terminal switching and view-local clear worked without stopping RTT; transport/backend drops stayed at 0. At a 768px viewport document width equaled the viewport and the terminal/control rows remained contained; browser warning/error logs were empty.

verification.area: Serial Assistant Web and paired virtual UART loop
verification.result: A Windows ELTIMA paired virtual serial fixture exercised the real OS serial API with concrete port identifiers intentionally omitted. A partial prompt produced an immediate terminal event before its later LF; ANSI color data, bare LF, CRLF, and a CSI sequence split across writes arrived exactly while structured Log events remained line-based. Reverse TX matched all 18 expected bytes for ASCII plus CRLF, binary 00 AA 55 FF, Enter, Backspace, and ArrowUp; terminal events preserved TX for statistics while the UI remains RX-only. Explicit stop released the OS port, reconnect reset counters and restored traffic, ended SSE subscribers did not stop acquisition, a second native open was denied, and 500 fixed-size lines delivered 3,000 of 3,000 bytes with 500 of 500 rows. Repeated CLI sends passed after the byte-zero lock fix; released lock markers report no owner. Modbus access to the occupied serial port returned HTTP 409 and left Serial Assistant open. Automated coverage still verifies no MKLink gate, separate send history, no local TX echo, status recovery, mode-local clear, and no stop on unmount; disconnected desktop and 768px Web layouts have no overflow or page errors.

verification.area: Dashboard Device ownership and independent serial lifecycle
verification.result: On the STM32 target, RTT and Serial Assistant ran concurrently. Stopping RTT while it was the last running MKLink-dependent Dashboard left Device connected and Serial Assistant running. The persistent header Disconnect action then stopped RTT and released Device while Serial Assistant stayed open and transmitted again through the real Windows serial API. Header quick connect restored the last successful probe and target settings without affecting Serial Assistant. Explicit Serial Assistant Close released its OS port for immediate native reopen while Device remained connected; final explicit header Disconnect left Device and all Dashboards stopped with an empty resource map.

verification.area: HPM6E00 composite-CDC discovery fix and online-flash HIL
verification.result: On fix/hpm-multi-interface-port, a real composite USB probe confirmed that shared CDC serial numbers made the old resolver choose by enumeration order; same-serial candidates now undergo an MKLink protocol handshake. The source Web GUI then exposed a second defect: browser uploads retained an old 36,932-byte File snapshot, and selecting the same path again did not fire change. Chromium/Edge selection now retains a read-only file handle, polls size plus lastModified every second, and uploads a fresh File when the build changes; the legacy input is cleared after each selection so same-path manual reload always emits. Regression coverage verified a retained handle causes a second inspection with rebuilt bytes. The maintainer's SEGGER Embedded Studio demo.bin was 35,052 bytes at 0x80000400 with SHA-256 bf9d5c79c10bc729bce2cf2dbb197e42ad0e7ff8d5c28ce8f896289ac2cd7388. A real HPM6E00 online-flash job completed connect, ROM-API program, verify, reset, and disconnect at 10 MHz with that exact size and digest. A read-only automatic reconnect selected the protocol-valid CDC interface, returned IDCODE 0x1000563d, and the first 16 Flash bytes exactly matched the BIN before disconnect. GUI passed 49 files and 497 tests; vue-tsc and Vite 8.1.5 production build passed. Python raw full reached 1,239 passed and 1 skipped with the same 12 Windows symlink-privilege failures and 3 missing-STCP-DLL packaging errors; the comparable gate passed 1,239 with 1 skipped and 15 explicit deselections. The source Vite server serves the tracked-picker implementation. Windows browser automation was unavailable, so the maintainer still needs to confirm the visible auto-refresh interaction. The qualified changes are committed and pushed to the origin fix branch; no merge, tag, or release was performed.
verification.area: CST92F41 relative Pack FLM geometry
verification.result: The installed Chipsea CST92Fxx Pack declares a 1 MiB PDSC flash region at 0x00400000 while its FLM declares the same 1 MiB device and 4 KiB sectors from 0x0. The old static intersection and pyOCD FlmFlashRegionBuilder therefore both produced no usable sector geometry. A bounded compatibility rule now rebases only non-overlapping FLM ranges that fit wholly inside the owning PDSC region, and the runtime copies the FLM before changing its start so shared Pack metadata is not mutated. The customer Intel HEX digest 86c75c18600af4cd71f68a65ea72c41d0a8c3c0699c67bdf2299658fdecd5eba spans 0x00404000-0x0043CEEC. Static inspection and a real pyOCD FLM finalisation produced 4 KiB geometry; the Web GUI showed FLM verified, 57 selected sectors from 0x00404000 through 0x0043C000, and an enabled Start Flash button with no console errors. Online-flash focused coverage passed 195 tests; full GUI passed 49 files and 494 tests; vue-tsc and Vite 8.1.5 production build passed. Python raw full reached 1,242 passed and 1 skipped with the same 12 Windows symlink-privilege failures and 3 missing-STCP-DLL package errors; the comparable gate passed 1,242 with 1 skipped and 15 explicit deselections. No CST target erase, program, reset, or hardware connection was performed.

Focused stream performance passed 15 tests and the frontend stream gate passed 5 tests.

verification.area: GUI simplification, resource arbitration, and Windows low-COM lock gate
verification.result: On fix/ui-resource-serial-com1, the Web/Tauri header and configuration status no longer expose detected MCU-family labels, Dashboard no longer offers the Debug Control tab, and the Taobao entry is an ordered menu containing the existing official store plus a disabled pending Xianji custom-store entry. A real 390x844 browser viewport confirmed the horizontally scrollable navigation, non-wrapping labels, and fully visible fixed-position store menu. A real STM32F103RC source Web session connected with builtin AXF parsing, started RTOS Trace, rendered named tasks and live events, then read 64 bytes through Memory; the read synchronously stopped Trace and left both mklink_bridge and target_debug leases empty. No flash, erase, reset, halt, resume, or write was performed. Windows low-number serial qualification created an ordinary serial_-prefixed lock path and completed serial send/log against an available single-digit virtual port. Raw full Python reached 1,253 passed and 1 skipped with only the 12 known WinError 1314 directory-symlink privilege failures; the exact reduced gate passed 1,253 with 1 skipped and 12 deselected. Full GUI passed 52 files and 507 tests; vue-tsc, Vite 8.1.5 production build, Tauri Builder prerequisite check, and git diff check passed.

decisions: The main Windows Tauri GUI exposes Site Agent configuration only in the native runtime. Its remote listener runs inside the existing Python sidecar and shares the current GUI Device and ResourceManager; Web-only GUI builds do not expose native credential controls. The standalone portable Site Agent remains a separately runnable EXE/ZIP for field-only deployments.

The main Tauri process owns every bundled sidecar generation through a Windows Job Object. Restart and shutdown close that Job before launching a replacement, so PyInstaller one-file workers cannot outlive their tracked launcher or retain the API/Agent ports.

Restoring a shared Device connection without an AXF is valid. The backend reparses symbols only when an active or requested AXF path exists; restore_last must not turn an already-connected probe into a No AXF path set failure.

Main-GUI Site Agent configuration is stored in LocalAppData, while the access token and STCP credentials are DPAPI CurrentUser ciphertext. Plaintext is generated or entered only for provisioning, never returned by status APIs or placed on command lines, and inherited Site Agent/STCP environment variables are removed before controlled child injection.

Product version 0.1.6 is one coordinated release across Python, plugin, main Tauri, standalone Tauri, core and portable package metadata, and GUI history. A complete Release contains five payloads—NSIS, updater signature, Skill ZIP, portable ZIP, and portable manifest—plus SHA256SUMS.txt and release-manifest.json.

A field machine may run Site Agent from the integrated main Windows GUI when local GUI workflows are needed, or from the standalone portable EXE for field-only deployment. Engineer machines use the Skill, SDK, remote CLI, or optional remote MCP over authenticated direct ws/wss or managed LAN/VPN transport.

Non-loopback remote listeners require explicit --allow-lan and token configuration. Tokens come only from environment variables or owner-only files, and local operator confirmation remains mandatory for flash, erase, writes, activation, and Agent stop.
LAN STCP uses the pinned in-process library bridge. No frpc/frps executable is launched or packaged, and tunnel, Site Agent, and local confirmation credentials remain distinct.

Any combined-runtime change after the fork's ddf7ff27 qualification invalidates its deterministic package hashes and HIL verdict for release purposes; the integration branch must be rebuilt and requalified before merge or publication.

The source Vite development server must proxy both REST /api traffic and binary /ws WebSocket upgrades to the same local backend. Any new browser transport prefix requires an explicit development-proxy contract test so source-Web behavior cannot silently diverge from the bundled backend surface.

AGENTS.md and the repository maintenance Skill are authoritative. Before changing a product, interaction, architecture, workflow, or testing strategy, present the problem, options, tradeoffs, recommendation, and acceptance criteria, then wait for explicit maintainer confirmation. Confirmed-strategy root-cause fixes may proceed directly. Runtime changes require a fix/feature branch, full Python and GUI suites, production build, git diff check, project-memory update, and affected real-hardware loop. Never infer authority to commit, merge, push, sign, tag, publish, modify latest.json, or synchronize Gitee.

HPM targets always use the dedicated ROM API and never FLM. Agent-driven download routing is IDE-native build/download, then pyOCD online flash, then MKLink offline deployment; do not silently switch after a started operation fails.

Builtin pyelftools is the default ELF/DWARF backend. External GNU tools run only when explicitly selected. _SEGGER_RTT in ELF/AXF is accepted only when its complete storage lies in an allocated writable section.

Symbol reload is one shared backend transaction bound to the current Device. Requested and active paths must match, and SuperWatch must be stopped/rebound/restarted serially. Pasted C layouts remain bounded and fingerprint-scoped.

Large arrays page by 256 direct elements, represented as explicit [start..end] range nodes that load only when expanded. Paging is recursive for structure and nested arrays. Exact search resolves unloaded paths through the backend, and dynamically resolved descriptors remain valid for SuperWatch, type lookup, and read/write. Do not restore a first-256-readable-leaves limit or its UI warning.

Dashboard sessions and one-shot debug/flash operations use serialized resource leases. User operations may preempt Dashboard owners only after synchronous stop succeeds; one user operation never preempts another. HPM online flash also closes the shared CDC Device before opening its ROM-API backend.

Desktop and Web-entry clients stop only backend processes they created and still own. Web app shells use no-store, hashed assets may be immutable, and copied user-level Skill/runtime installations must not depend on the development checkout.

SuperWatch uses a fixed-duration timeline independent of history capacity, defaults to zoom 2 at the newest window, and supports up to 1,000,000 points/channel with a 48-byte-per-point memory estimate and a warning above 512 MiB. Live horizontal interactions preserve the chosen time lag and span while advancing; pause freezes the complete frontend history and viewport; resume clears the snapshot; double-click restores the newest default window. VOFA retains its adaptive timeline.

SuperWatch effective rate counts complete sample rows rather than variables and never uses the requested interval as the result. The backend uses a one-second perf_counter window as the authoritative status value; the binary viewer uses producer batch timestamps over at least 0.5 seconds for responsive updates between status polls and resets the statistic at stream/layout boundaries.

SuperWatch defaults to one shared plot. One visible channel may move to a lower plot with an independent persisted Y range while both plots share X navigation. The auto-hiding legend uses a compact reveal button, and a persistent split divider names the independent channel and provides Merge.

The global GUI language defaults to Chinese and persists under mklink_lang. English technical product names are not translated. Post-flash reconnection was explicitly canceled and must not be inferred.

RTT View is intentionally fixed to channel 0 with a compact 日志 | 终端 mode switch. Log and terminal use independent binary subscribers and Worker decode paths. Terminal mode uses xterm.js with convertEol, common ANSI/SEGGER normalization, and Down Buffer keyboard forwarding, but it must not construct or synchronize hidden log data. Log mode is capped at 5,000 retained entries, uses VirtualLogPanel windowing, and may save only those retained entries as a timestamped UTF-8 .log file. Backend bytes remain unchanged. Do not add termios, PTY/ConPTY, multi-channel UI, or SEGGER virtual-terminal support without a new confirmed strategy.

Serial Assistant is independent of MKLink deviceConnected and uses the SERIAL_PORT resource while RTT uses MKLINK_BRIDGE/TARGET_DEBUG. One bounded backend hub preserves immediate exact RX/TX chunks; separate Worker clients decode either Log or Terminal mode. Terminal displays RX only, forwards raw keyboard bytes without local echo, and must not construct or synchronize hidden log data. Log mode is capped at 5,000 retained entries, uses VirtualLogPanel windowing, and may save only those retained entries as a timestamped UTF-8 .log file. Mode/tab/route changes preserve the backend session and close only the browser subscription; explicit Close Port is authoritative. Physical UART and Modbus access to one COM port must still fail clearly rather than run concurrently.

Starting or stopping an MKLink-dependent Dashboard never owns the shared Device lifetime. The persistent Dashboard header Connect Device / Disconnect control is the authoritative normal Web owner: Connect restores the last successful actual probe port, AXF path, MCU hint, and ELF backend; Disconnect synchronously stops only MKLink-dependent Dashboards, releases their logical leases, and closes Device. Serial Assistant and Modbus remain independent and are never stopped by Device Disconnect. Dashboard tab, route, mode, and stream-subscriber changes remain non-owning.

Contextual setup guidance appears where work is blocked and offers the next useful action. Device-only tools prompt quick connect; RTT and RTOS Trace offer AXF/ELF loading for RTT address discovery; SuperWatch and Symbols distinguish missing, stale, empty, and failed symbol states; HardFault keeps symbols optional; RTOS Trace keeps offline JSONL replay available; Serial Assistant and Modbus guide missing serial-port setup without depending on Device.

Offline Flash serializes only algorithms referenced by firmware rows. Unused unavailable FLM candidates must not block deployment; a selected unavailable candidate must be visibly actionable through local replacement or another algorithm, and backend text remains available under technical details. RTT View and Serial Assistant default to Terminal mode. External documentation/store links display labels only and open with target=_blank plus noopener noreferrer. Family-level MCU IDCODE matches must not claim uncertain density/package qualifiers.

Windows serial advisory locks always lock byte zero and clear their PID marker before unlock, so repeated open/close cycles do not raise and released resources are not reported as live. Modbus Dashboard opens through ModbusClient.open and returns HTTP 409 when the requested serial port is busy or unavailable.

RTT View and RTOS Trace share one valid RTT address. SystemView uses SystemView.start plus the SEGGER recorder handshake and matching stop sequence on both ARM/SWD and HPM RISC-V/JTAG. START supplies INIT/SYSDESC/SYSTIME, delayed TaskList recovers startup metadata, ram_base=0 and id_shift=0 are valid, and late attach hydrates task, ISR, clock, drop, and recording metadata from backend status.

SystemView uses complete bounded intervals for exact Runtime/Context analysis, retains inactive contexts, keeps 60 seconds of exact history and a 300,000-event browser ring, and offers 10/30/60-second views. JSONL recording is independent of display/acquisition, and offline replay is incremental and bounded with pause, speed, progress, and restart.
MCP stdio reserves stdout for JSON-RPC. Ordinary Python output is redirected to stderr only for the MCP entry; CLI, Web, and desktop logging remain unchanged.

Composite MKLink USB CDC interfaces can share one serial number. When a probe serial identifier maps to multiple ports, discovery must perform the MKLink protocol handshake on each candidate and never choose by COM-number or enumeration order.

Browser online flash uses the File System Access API when available to retain a read-only firmware handle for the current page session and poll rebuilt-file metadata. Unsupported browsers use a fresh normal file selection, and every fallback input clears its value so choosing the same path reloads the file. Browser clients never persist or expose the local absolute path.

When a Pack PDSC flash region and its embedded FLM address range do not overlap, the FLM may be treated as region-relative only if its complete range fits within the PDSC region. Static sector inspection and pyOCD runtime finalisation must use this same bounded mapping. Runtime relocation copies the FLM object and never disables the sector-geometry safety gate.

Detected MCU-family names are backend facts but are not user-facing status labels. Target selectors remain available where the exact part is required. Dashboard omits destructive Debug Control UI while preserving CLI/API debugging. Windows serial lock files always use a non-reserved serial_ prefix and the serial helper shares the local resource path implementation; failure to create the advisory lock must return a normal unavailable result rather than crash or silently bypass mutual exclusion.

The header store entry is one responsive details menu. The official store keeps its established URL; the Xianji custom-store entry remains visibly disabled until the maintainer supplies an authoritative URL.

hardware.probe: Fresh v0.1.6 GEC1900 qualification used a real MKLink CDC probe and detected the MICROKEEN removable drive. Concrete port and device identifiers remain intentionally omitted.
hardware.target: Fresh v0.1.6 GEC1900 qualification recognized an STM32F40x through the main GUI, unified Site Agent, and engineer CLI. The HPM6E00 EVK hello_world image was rebuilt and successfully programmed, verified, reset, and read back through the HPM ROM API. The CST92F41 customer Pack and image were qualified through static inspection, real FLM finalisation, and Web GUI without connecting to or changing a CST target. Existing STM32F103RC and HPM5301 EVK Lite evidence remains recorded.
hardware.serial_fixture: A paired ELTIMA virtual serial-port fixture is available. The HPM6E00 hello_world USB serial output also passed a 10-minute real-target high-rate Web terminal soak; concrete COM numbers are intentionally omitted.
hardware.permission: Firmware build/flash and read-only target validation are permitted when required by the active task.

known_limits: The maintainer host has an established local Tauri updater private key and the v0.1.6 installer was signed for local qualification. Official publication still requires separate maintainer authorization; do not change tags, releases, updater manifests, or Gitee state implicitly.

The v0.1.6 branch passed direct LAN Site Agent automation and fresh STM32 hardware qualification, but external managed-LAN STCP was not rerun because no independent LAN frps endpoint was available. The imported fork STCP/HIL evidence remains supplementary rather than fresh v0.1.6 proof.

High-event-rate SystemView can overflow the target RTT buffer. Host TaskList retry recovers metadata, but physically dropped event packets cannot be reconstructed; increase the target buffer for loss-sensitive timing analysis.
The first real V4 offline trigger once returned a transient empty failure and an immediate retry succeeded. Reproduce cold starts and add device-output diagnostics if it recurs.
Full npm audit reports one high-severity development-only transitive finding in brace-expansion; the runtime dependency audit is clean.

Serial Assistant's closed loop used a paired virtual serial driver and therefore does not qualify USB-UART electrical behavior, cable faults, or adapter-specific driver latency; the host software and Windows serial API path are qualified.

Automatic rebuilt-firmware detection in browser mode requires the Chromium File System Access API and a handle selected during the current page session. Unsupported browsers and reloaded pages require one manual file selection. Browser and installed-desktop same-path selection are both supported and were confirmed with the supplied STM32F103RC HEX.

The CST92F41 relative-FLM fix has real Pack, customer-image, pyOCD finalisation, and Web interaction evidence, but no physical CST92 target was available for erase/program/verify HIL. This merge uses the maintainer's explicit hardware-gate waiver; future physical CST release evidence remains pending.
The Xianji custom-store URL has not been supplied, so its menu entry is intentionally disabled and no guessed link is shipped.

USB Web entry still needs macOS/Linux qualification. Standard NSIS and updater behavior still need a second clean Windows machine. Non-builtin flash algorithm paths have automated coverage but limited physical-target coverage.
next_actions: Provide the established Tauri updater signing key for a full NSIS release, or explicitly authorize a GitHub Release limited to the portable/Skill integrity assets without the signed updater installer.

Reproduce the first-trigger V4 offline empty failure across cold starts and add device-output diagnostics if it recurs.
Run loss-sensitive SystemView tests with a larger target RTT buffer and document the sustainable event rate.
Qualify USB Web entry on current macOS and Linux systems.
Qualify standard NSIS and older-client updater behavior on a clean Windows 10/11 machine.
